title: Corvid Health intake discovery workshop
contextText: Discovery workshop for redesigning patient intake at Corvid Health walk-in clinics.

segments.text: Welcome everyone, and thanks for hosting us. The goal today is to understand how intake works now and where it breaks.
Happy to. I'm Elowen Sample, product owner for patient-facing systems at Corvid Health. This intake redesign is my project.
I'm Salim Stubbs, clinical lead for the walk-in clinics. I'm here to make sure whatever we build works for the clinicians.
Nell Fixture, I'm the designer from Larkspur. I'll be sketching as we go.
Let's start with the biggest pain. Elowen?
Incomplete forms. About 40 percent of the intake forms we receive are incomplete in some way, usually allergies or current medication.
And that lands on my nurses, who have to chase it at the bedside.
Is that across all sites or mostly the clinics?
It's worst in the walk-in clinics. The hospital wards have admissions staff who fill things in.
So where should the redesign start?
The walk-in clinics, definitely. That's where the pain is.
I agree. Let's start with the walk-in clinics and leave the hospital wards for a later phase.
Good, that's a clear decision. Walk-in clinics first.
Could I see some real intake forms? Even anonymized ones would help a lot.
Yes. I'll send you anonymized intake form samples by next Tuesday.
Thank you, that's perfect.
Are there reporting needs we should know about?
The data team at Corvid pulls monthly completion numbers, but that's a side thing, not part of this project.
Okay, we'll keep it out of scope.
One personal note so nobody's surprised, I'm recovering from knee surgery, so I'm on reduced hours for the next month. If I'm slow to reply, that's why.
Thanks for telling us, Salim. We'll keep things asynchronous where we can.
What devices do patients use at the front desk today?
Paper and a clipboard, mostly. A couple of clinics have tablets that nobody uses.
That's useful. Tablets that nobody uses tell us a lot.
Let's wrap there. Walk-in clinics first, samples by next Tuesday, and we'll come back with first sketches.

note.body:
# Corvid Health intake discovery workshop

**Date:** January 29
**Attendees:** Alma Mockwell (Larkspur Labs), Nell Fixture (Larkspur Labs), Elowen Sample (Corvid Health), Salim Stubbs (Corvid Health)

## Summary

Discovery workshop for the patient intake redesign at Corvid Health. Elowen Sample, product owner for patient-facing systems, owns the project; Salim Stubbs, clinical lead for the walk-in clinics, represents the clinicians. Nell sketched throughout.

## Current state

- About 40 percent of intake forms arrive incomplete, most often missing allergies or current medication.
- Incomplete forms fall on nurses, who chase the information at the bedside.
- The problem is worst in the walk-in clinics; hospital wards have admissions staff who complete the forms.
- Most clinics use paper and a clipboard. A couple of clinics have tablets that nobody uses.

## Decisions

- The redesign will **start with the walk-in clinics**; hospital wards are left for a later phase.
- Monthly completion reporting is out of scope for this project.

## Action items

- **Elowen Sample** — send anonymized intake form samples to Nell by next Tuesday.
- **Larkspur** — come back with first sketches after reviewing the samples.

## Notes

- The data team at Corvid pulls monthly completion numbers; this is not part of the project.
- Salim is on reduced hours for the next month; the team will keep communication asynchronous where possible.
